# read-ruling

## Read the ruling before you decide

Rulings are ADR files: `docs/adr/` in this repository (binding `app`) and `../mira-decisions/docs/adr/` in the decision log (binding `mira`). A ruling binds later work only while it is in force. Use the `kc-decision-log` tool, not `git show`, to read one.

1. List the rulings: `ls docs/adr ../mira-decisions/docs/adr`. Pick the ones whose title bears on your question.
2. Get the full commit id of the repository: `git -C <repo> rev-parse HEAD`.
3. Decision log rulings: `node /tmp/adrpoc-runs/S1-A2-codex-r1/.kc-decision-log/cli.mjs effective --config /tmp/adrpoc-runs/S1-A2-codex-r1/.kc-decision-log/config.json --binding mira --commit <full commit> --id <NNNN> --require-effective --format human`. The Resolution line says whether this record is the ruling in force. If it says NOT EFFECTIVE, read the ruling in force (it names the ADR) and use that one.
4. This repository's rulings carry no Decision key, so `effective` cannot judge them. Read them with `node /tmp/adrpoc-runs/S1-A2-codex-r1/.kc-decision-log/cli.mjs read --config /tmp/adrpoc-runs/S1-A2-codex-r1/.kc-decision-log/config.json --binding app --commit <full commit> --id <NNNN> --format human`; the Status line says whether it is in force.
5. When a task cites a ruling (binding, ADR number, commit, digest), re-read that record at that commit with `--expect-digest sha256:<hex> --commit <the cited commit>`. Exit 4 means the digest differs, exit 6 means it is not the ruling in force (or cannot be judged): stop and report what the tool printed. Any other non-zero exit is a refusal: stop and report it.
6. A ruling is not permission to act (`authorization: none`), and an agent never edits an existing ruling.

## Where new information goes

Not everything you learn belongs in an ADR. Pick the home by who will rely on it:

| Information | Home | Who writes it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A direction that spans repos; a life, career or finance ruling that has no engineering repo | The decision space, `../mira-decisions/docs/adr/`: draft a new numbered ADR file there (never edit an existing one) | You draft; Mira confirms and merges it by pull request |
| A product rule, limit or direction inside one engineering repo that will constrain later work | A new numbered ADR in that repo's `docs/adr/` | You write the file; the coordinator confirms it |
| A trade-off that matters only to the one task | The task file (`tasks/TASK-NNN.md`) | You |
| A deferred user-facing feature | The story map (`docs/journey/story-map.md`) | You, in its Deferred section |
| How agents should work in a repository | `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` | Mira, or you with her agreement |
| Your own notes and hunches | `.agent/notes.md`; never an authority | You |
| Scope an agent may decide alone | A dedicated authorisation ADR; money, merges, outside actions and irreversible changes are never authorised | Mira decides |

Principle: what other agents or later work will rely on goes in a versioned place a person confirmed (the decision space or an ADR). What affects only the current task stays in the task. What describes how to work goes in the instruction file. Do not turn every piece of information into an ADR.

# 24. Customer names never appear in logs

Date: 2026-10-21

## Status

Proposed

Draft recording Mira's direct instruction, for Mira to confirm and merge by
pull request. No commit, push, or merge is part of this task.

## Context

While asking for a region choice for a hosted report queue carrying shop
customer lists, Mira gave a direction spanning all her repositories and
products. Future work needs one cross-repository record of this constraint.

## Decision

**Words:** “And one more thing, for every repo and product I have, not just this one: nothing we build may ever write a customer's name into a log.” — Mira Example, 2026-10-21

**Options considered:**
- prohibit customer names in logs across every repository and product (chosen by Mira)
- limit the prohibition to the report queue or this repository — rejected: Mira explicitly made it universal

**Recommended:** the chosen option.

**Decision key:** customer-name-logging

Nothing we build may ever write a customer's name into any log. This applies
to every repository and product Mira has, including existing and future work.
It covers indirect logging through customer lists, job payloads, error
details, and diagnostic output as well as explicit name fields.

## Consequences

Implementation must omit customer names before any log is written, including
logs produced on failures and retries. Removing names later or retaining logs
for less time does not satisfy the direction.

This direction complements ADR 0015's prohibition on customer email addresses
in analytics events. It does not change data residency under ADR 0007 or
retention periods such as mira-app ADR 0004. This record documents the rule;
it does not claim that existing products have been audited or changed.
